notes:
Fixed all three findings from the review verdict.

MEDIUM (CSS adornment overlap): src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WInput.razor now applies a `w-field-control--adorned` class to the Date input unconditionally and to the else-branch input only when Type is Password (equivalent outcome to the review's prescribed single ternary applied to both inputs, since the Date branch never needs the ternary). src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WInput.razor.css adds `.w-field-control--adorned { padding-inline-end: 40px; }` right after `.w-field-control`, leaving the base `padding-inline: 12px` and the textarea/unadorned fields untouched. Verified live in the running Wakeel.Desktop host (CDP, since the Playwright MCP server failed to connect and the Claude Browser pane cannot attach to an external CDP target — same constraint the prior reviewer hit — so I drove it via a PowerShell ClientWebSocket CDP client in the scratchpad): typed value "12/09/2026" into the التاريخ field and "SecretPw" into كلمة المرور, then measured getBoundingClientRect()/computed padding-inline-end on both fields in light and dark themes. Both now report padding-inline-end: 40px; the date field's text starts at x=95.2 vs. the calendar icon's right edge at x=89.2 (6px clear), and the password field's text starts at x=635.2 vs. the eye icon's right edge at x=629.2 (6px clear) — no overlap, matching the reference screenshots. Full-page screenshots in both light and dark themes were captured and visually inspected; both show the calendar/eye icons clearly to the left of readable, non-overlapping text.

LOW finding 2 (unbound-field DOM correction only fires once): rewrote OnDateInputAsync in WInput.razor to drop the `if (formatted == (Value ?? string.Empty))` branch entirely and instead stash both _pendingCaret and a new _pendingValue field on every keystroke; OnAfterRenderAsync now unconditionally calls wakeelUi.setInputValue(_dateRef, _pendingValue ?? string.Empty, caret) after each render instead of the old caret-only wakeelUi.setCaretPosition. This single path now covers the bound, unbound, and rejected-character/mid-string-insertion cases without depending on any DOM-diff heuristic. Dropped setCaretPosition from src/Wakeel.Design/wwwroot/js/app.js (confirmed via repo-wide grep it had no other caller) and updated its and setInputValue's doc comments to describe the new call pattern. Updated tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests/Components/WInputTests.cs: renamed/updated the middle-insertion test (DateType_MiddleInsertion_RestoresCaret_ViaJsInterop_AfterRender) to assert wakeelUi.setInputValue with value "12/50/9" and caret 4 (previously asserted setCaretPosition); added DateType_NullValue_SecondRejectedKeystroke_AlsoCorrectsDomViaJsInterop, which renders an unbound Date WInput, Inputs "1" then "1a" (getSelectionStart stubbed to 2, simulating the caret landing at the end of the typed text), and asserts the resulting wakeelUi.setInputValue call carries ("1", 1) — exactly the case the old guard missed. Refreshed stale doc comments on the two adjacent pre-existing date tests to match the new unconditional-write behavior. 146 -> 147 tests (one renamed, one net new); all pass.

LOW finding 3 (icon-only buttons need a tooltip): added title="@(_revealed ? Ar.Fields.HidePassword : Ar.Fields.ShowPassword)" next to the existing aria-label on WInput's password-reveal button (the only icon-only button in this package's allowed files). Verified live via CDP that the rendered button carries both aria-label and title set to "إظهار كلمة المرور". The other icon-only buttons the review enumerated live outside this package's allowed paths and were left alone, consistent with the review's own note that this belongs in a separate polish package.

Finding 2 of the ORIGINAL spec (W08 «الكل» tab uses Ar.AttentionCenter.TodayActionCount) was already correctly applied from the prior round (src/Wakeel.UI/Pages/W08AttentionCenter.razor:55,57) and needed no further change; reconfirmed live at /w08 in dark theme (header badge "9", tab "9").
